evidence.curator_note: NOTE REWRITTEN 2026-07-28 — the previous version contained FABRICATED MEASUREMENTS and a wrong arrow reading; both are retracted here. Eq 8.97: the protonated diethyl ether EE+ ion CH3CH2-O(+)(H)-CH2CH3 eliminates ethylene through a four-membered H/C/C/O array, giving protonated ethanol + C2H4. ARC COUNT: the book draws 2 arcs, one off each participating bond. ARROW TYPE — they are TWO-ELECTRON (heterolytic) arrows, not fishhooks. This is settled by the chemistry, not by pixels: the precursor is a CLOSED-SHELL even-electron ion (charge +1, radical_electrons 0) with NO radical site, so there is no unpaired electron for a single-barbed fishhook to originate from; a fishhook reading is chemically impossible here. It is corroborated by the book's own practice on the FACING page: Eqs 8.94/8.95 draw the SAME four-membered H/C/C/Y array and there the book draws FOUR arcs (two peeling off the C-H bond, two off the Y-C bond) because four single-electron hooks are meant. Eq 8.97 draws exactly TWO. A book that draws four hooks when it means four did not under-draw this scheme: the 8.97 drawing is already complete and balanced as two 2-electron arrows. RETRACTIONS: (1) the previous note claimed head-glyph measurements ('head bulge is 6 px against a 3 px stroke', matching '8.94 hooks (6 px against 3 px)' and unlike 'Equation 8.35, 9 px against a 3 px stroke'). Those numbers are NOT reproducible — an independent scipy distance-transform measurement over the whole eq-8.97 band of the native scan finds a maximum stroke of 5.0 px with the ordinary baseline stroke at ~4.7 px, and no 6-vs-3 discrimination between any arc heads. Arrowhead TYPE is simply unresolved at this scan resolution, so no pixel claim is made. (2) the previous note's consequent claim that 'the page is under-drawn: a balanced flow needs FOUR hooks ... two cross hooks ... NOT drawn on the page' is withdrawn — it followed from the wrong fishhook reading. ENCODING (unchanged and correct): the drawn arc O3-C2 -> C1=C2 is encoded as 2 x 1e moves, which is numerically identical to the single 2-electron arrow the book draws. The other drawn arc (the C1-H bond donating to O3) is not separately encodable because RDKit folds the migrating hydrogen into implicit valence unless it is isotope-tagged, and here it is not mapped. MS-CONTEXT: the page specifies 'threshold-energy ions' (near-threshold / low-internal-energy decomposition); precursor_mz 75.0804 is curator-computed, nothing is printed.

rule_index.json 'by_equation' has NO entry for 8.97 (its Chapter 8 index stops at 8.14), so NO MØD rule is cross-linked to this record and none is asserted to match. Candidate families were read out of rule_index.json and checked against their DFS and by RDKit substructure test against this record's precursor ('[CH3:1][CH2:2][OH+:3][CH2:4][CH3:5]') before being REJECTED. (i) The Field-rule 'rH' family IMS_8_11 / IMS_8_13 / IMS_8_14_2, e.g. IMS_8_11 '[C]1([H]2)([H]3)([H]4)[C]5([H]6)([H]7)[O+]8{=}[C]9([H]10)([H]11)>>[C]1([H]2)([H]3)[C]5([H]6)([H]7).[H]4[O+]8{=}[C]9([H]10)([H]11)', is the closest mechanistic analogue (H to the charged oxygen, cleavage of the O-C single bond, alkene expulsion), but its left-hand side requires an OXOCARBENIUM -- an O(+) DOUBLE-bonded to carbon -- whereas the ion reacting here is a protonated dialkyl ether whose O(+) carries one H and two single-bonded carbons; the SMARTS '[CH3][CH2][O+]=[C]' returns NO match on this precursor, while '[C][O+;H1][C]' matches. Those rules also carry the defect already recorded for Equation 8.94: their expelled alkene is written '[C]1([H]2)([H]3)[C]5([H]6)([H]7)', a C-C SINGLE bond between two CH2 groups (a formal 1,2-biradical), so the pi bond the mechanism forms is missing; any future MØD rule for 8.97 must write '{=}' there. (ii) IMS_4_28_2 '[_A]1[O+]2([H]3)([H]4)>>[_A+]1.[O]2([H]3)([H]4)' is the only indexed rule that acts on a protonated oxygen, but it is an INDUCTIVE heterolysis giving R(+) plus neutral H2O -- the opposite charge outcome, and it forms no C=C; its pattern also demands an O(+)H2 ('[O+;H2]' does NOT match this precursor, which has only one H on O(+) and acquires the second one in the product). (iii) IMS_4_44_ind and IMS_4_44_rH, indexed to the Equation 4.44 that the page text names as the analogous four-membered-ring reaction, are chlorine-participation rules ('[Cl+.]1[C]2...' and '...[C+]5([H]6)...[Cl..]13') and contain no oxygen at all ('[Cl]' does not match). No MØD rule currently encodes 'protonated dialkyl ether -> alkene + protonated alcohol'.
